content: Parapiptadenia rigida is a perennial plant that can grow either as a shrub or a tree. It is not considered a threatened species. This species is native to Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay. It is commonly referred to by various names, including Angico, Angico-cedro, Angico-do-banhado, Angico-dos-montes, Angico-verdadeiro, Angico-vermelho, Guarucaia, and Paric. The tree typically grows to a height of 18 to 30 meters and features a straight trunk with slightly furrowed bark. Its foliage is dark green, and its flowers are greenish-yellow, measuring between 5 and 9 centimeters in length. The tree blooms during the spring season. Its seed pods are 9 to 16 centimeters long, and the seeds themselves are flat, oval-shaped, and brown in color. Parapiptadenia rigida is commonly found along riverbanks. Uses Essential Oils The essential oils derived from this tree are increasingly recognized for their utility in the production of industrial fragrance products. Gum The gum extracted from Parapiptadenia rigida can be used as a substitute for gum arabic. Medicinal Uses This tree possesses a range of medicinal properties, including astringent, expectorant, anti-diarrheal, antiseptic, and hemorrhage-arresting effects. In southern Brazil, it is particularly valued for its antiseptic properties. In traditional folk medicine, it is used as a bitter tonic and body cleanser. It is also employed in the treatment of conditions such as rickets, loss of appetite, and muscle weakness. Additionally, Parapiptadenia rigida is known to have psychoactive properties. Wood The wood of Parapiptadenia rigida is dense, highly resistant to environmental factors, and is widely used in construction, carpentry, bridge beams, poles, and as firewood. It is notably resistant to insect damage, including termites, and can remain intact for over 20 years without being painted. The wood has a parallel bending strength of 16,900 psi, a parallel compression strength of 8,500 psi, and a density ranging from 720 to 1,199 kg/m³ at a moisture content of 12-15%. Its modulus of elasticity is 157,801 kg/cm². When used for hardwood flooring, it is marketed under the name Pepperwood.
